We should obtain the control name by using controlled_by association? And why are we appending the Device name to the control name of the redfish? Also check if function introduced in parent commit can be reused to resolve the association.

Done. ControlId is now just the prefix (e.g., ClockLimit) — removed makeControlName and the device name suffix. DataSourceUri now points to /redfish/v1/Chassis/{chassisId}/Controls/ClockLimit.

I think we don't need to use the controlled_by association here since the mapping from D-Bus interface to control prefix is a fixed compile-time table in control_utils.hpp. We already know the interface (Control.Processor) at this point, so we can look up the prefix directly without an extra D-Bus call. 
But if you'd prefer using the association for consistency, I'm happy to change it — please let me know.
Why are we calling this function here? Shouldn't it be called inside `getProcessorControlSpeedProperties`?
Done
Shouldn't we check if associated object path containing this control interface is present before populating the property?
Done. Thanks for the catch.
LGTM
Consider to use `sdbusplus::object_path` here
Most paths in processor.hpp (and bmcweb in general) use `const std::string&` for D-Bus object paths. Keeping consistent with that here — happy to revisit if you feel strongly about it.

Using `sdbusplus::object_path` is indeed nit and doesn't necessarily be applied.
Tracing back your code, I found that the source of using `const std::string&` instead of `sdbusplus::object_path` is within the `getProcessorData()`.

In this case, I think we could have a refactor patch to change the use of `const std::string&` to `sdbusplus::object_path&`.
Consider to use `sdbusplus::object_path` instead of `std::string`
Most paths in processor.hpp (and bmcweb in general) use `const std::string&` for D-Bus object paths. Keeping consistent with that here — happy to revisit if you feel strongly about it.

@andhsieh@nvidia.com
FYI, this is the part I think we can do the refactor for `objectPath`.

Is OperatingSpeedRangeMHz.DataSourceUri expected to remain stable across reboots or inventory re-enumeration, or should clients rediscover it for each boot/session? Please clarify the intended behavior.
